Q_001,How do I get help for food like SNAP or other places?,"## Getting Food Help in California

Losing a job can make it hard to put food on the table. California has several programs that can give you *free* or *low‑cost* food. Below is a simple guide to the most common options, who can qualify, what you need to apply, and how long it usually takes.
### 1. **CalFresh (California’s SNAP program)**

column3: Gives you an **Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT)** card that works like a debit card. You can buy most groceries at supermarkets, farmers markets, and many local stores.

- Anyone who lives in California
- Meets **income** limits (usually about 200 % of the federal poverty level) **or** has a qualifying disability/elder‑status
- Must be a U.S. citizen or have eligible immigration status (see county website for details)

1. **Online** – go to **[www.getcalfresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)** or **BenefitsCal.com** and create an account.
2. **Phone** – call the CalFresh Help Line **1‑877‑847‑3663**.
3. **In‑person** – visit your **County Social Services Agency** (e.g., Los Angeles County Department of Public Social Services).
4. **Mail** – you can print an application from the website and mail it to your county office.

- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Proof of California residency (utility bill, lease, or mailbox receipt)
- Recent pay stubs, unemployment benefits statement, or other income proof (including child support, SSI, etc.)
- Bank statements or a list of any money you have in cash, checking, savings, or investments
- Social Security numbers for everyone in the household
Most counties review applications within **30 days**. If you need food right now, you can request **Emergency CalFresh**, which can give you a temporary EBT card in as few as **5‑7 days**.

Every California county runs its own CalFresh office, so **phone numbers and office hours can differ**. Look up your county’s contact info on the **[California Department of Social Services (CDSS) county list](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Social-Services-Directory)**.

column1: ### 2. **Women, Infants & Children (WIC)**

column3: Provides nutritious foods (milk, cheese, eggs, fruits, vegetables, infant formula, and more) *plus* nutrition counseling for pregnant people, new parents, and kids under 5.
Pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding people, and children up to age 5 who meet income guidelines (about 185 % of the federal poverty level).
Call your local **County Health Department** or **WIC clinic**. You can also start online at **[WIC California](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CFH/Pages/WIC.aspx)**.

- Photo ID
- Proof of pregnancy or birth certificate for the child
- Proof of income (pay stub, unemployment benefits, etc.)
- Proof of California residency
After the first appointment, you usually get a **WIC card** the same day and can start using it at approved stores.

column1: ### 3. **Local Food Banks & Pantries**

column3: Food banks collect and distribute free groceries. You can pick up food boxes or go to a pantry without an application.

• Call **2‑1‑1** (or dial **211** on your phone) for a list of nearby food banks and pantry hours.
• Visit **[Feeding America’s food bank locator](https://www.feedingamerica.org/find-your-local-foodbank)** for a map of agencies in California.
• Many county social services websites also list local food pantries.
Typically just a **photo ID** and proof of residence (like a utility bill) for verification, but many places will serve you even without these documents.
Most food banks operate **weekly** or **monthly**; some have same‑day drop‑off for emergency needs. Call ahead to confirm hours.

Yes! In California you can usually receive several public‑assistance programs together (for example, food benefits **and** health coverage). Each program has its own rules, so you’ll need to check the details for the programs you want and tell each office about the other help you are getting.

## Steps to Get Multiple Benefits
1. **Make a list** of the programs you think you might qualify for (e.g., CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, GA, SSI).
2. **Apply for each one** – you can often do them at the same time online or in person.
* CalFresh & Medi‑Cal: apply together at your county **Human Services** office or online at [BenefitsCalWIN](https://benefits.calwin.org).
* GA (General Assistance): go to your **county social services** office (search “General Assistance *your county*”).
* SSI: start at the **Social Security Administration** website or call 1‑800‑772‑1213.
3. **Tell every program about the others** when you fill out the application.
4. **Gather the same basic paperwork** for each (see the table below).
5. **Wait for decisions** – most applications are processed within 30‑45 days, but timelines can vary by county.

## County‑Specific Note

Every county in California runs its own **Human Services** or **Social Services** office. While the rules for CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, and SSI are statewide, things like **General Assistance amounts, cash‑aid time limits, and required paperwork** can differ.

*Look up your county’s website* (e.g., “Alameda County Social Services” or “Los Angeles County CalFresh”) and read the **“Apply”** section. If anything is unclear, call the **intake line**—they can tell you which forms are required locally.

### 4. Step‑by‑Step Action Plan (Do This Today)
1. **Call 2‑1‑1** (or visit **[211.org](https://www.211.org)**) and ask for “Emergency Rental Assistance in *your county*”. Write down the phone number or website they give you.
2. **Gather the documents** listed above. If you don’t have something, ask the agency how you can replace it (e.g., a “letter of verification” from your landlord).

- **California ERAP is run by each county**, so the exact income limits, required forms, and processing times can differ.

column1: ## How to Put It All Together
1. **Apply for UI right away** – even if you think you might not qualify, the EDD will tell you.
2. **Ask the EDD about CTB** while you’re filing UI.  If you find a training program you like, the EDD can approve you to keep benefits.

3. **Contact your County Human Services Agency** (CHSA) to see if you qualify for CalWORKs, CalFresh, or Medi‑Cal.  Many counties have one “one‑stop” office where you can start all three applications.
4. **Look for local job‑training options** – check:
* **CalWORKs job‑placement & training** office
* **Community colleges** (many have “career technical education” programs)
* **Workforce Development Boards** (county‑specific, often list free apprenticeships)
5. **Keep records** of every form you submit, the date, and any confirmation numbers.  This helps if you need to follow up later.
6. **Certify UI each week** – even while you’re in training or waiting for other benefits.  Missing a week can delay payments.

When you lose a job in California, the **Unemployment Insurance (UI) program** can give you a temporary paycheck.

There isn’t a single “income‑limit” like a set dollar amount you can’t exceed. Instead, you must **have earned enough wages during a specific “base period”** (the first four of the last five completed calendar quarters) to qualify.
## Who Can Get UI?

column1: *These rules are the same across California, but **some counties may have extra help programs**, so it’s a good idea to check with your local Employment Development Department (EDD) office.
## How the Base‑Period Earnings Work
1. **Find your base period** – It’s the first four quarters of the last five completed calendar quarters.
*Example:* If you apply in November 2025, the base period is **January 1 2023 through December 31 2023**.
2. **Calculate total wages** – Add up all wages you earned (including tips, overtime, and certain non‑cash benefits) during that period.
3. **Meet the earnings test** –
* You must have earned **at least $1,300 total** in the base period **or**
* Earned **at least $900** in your highest‑earning quarter **and** at least **$1,500 total** in the base period.
*(These numbers are the current statutory minimums; they can change each year, so double‑check the latest UI calculator on the EDD website.)*

If you meet either of those tests, you are **eligible** for UI benefits. The amount you receive each week is based on a formula that looks at your highest‑earning quarter, not on a set “income limit.”
## Steps to Apply
1. **Gather required documents**
- Social Security number
- Proof of identity (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Recent pay stubs or a **W‑2** for the last year (shows your wages)
- Your **most recent employer’s contact info** (name, address, phone)
2. **Create an online UI account** at the EDD portal:
- Go to **[edd.ca.gov/unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)**
- Click **“Apply Now”** and follow the prompts
3. **Complete the application** – Answer questions about your work history, reason for separation, and availability for work.
4. **Submit your claim** – You’ll get a confirmation number.
5. **Certify each week** – Log in each week (or use the UI Phone System) to confirm you’re still unemployed and looking for work.
6. **Watch for communications** – The EDD will email or mail any requests for more information. Respond quickly to avoid delays.

column1: ### Step 3 – Fill Out the Application
1. **Personal info:** name, address, phone, SSN, ID number.
2. **Work history:** list every employer you had in the past 18 months (including part‑time and temporary jobs).
3. **Reason you’re not working:** e.g., laid off, reduced hours, quit for good cause, etc.
4. **Bank info** for direct deposit (highly recommended).
### Step 4 – Register for UI Online (myEDD)
- After you submit the claim, the EDD will mail you a **Customer Account Number** (usually within a few days).
- Use that number to register for **UI Online**. This portal lets you:
- Certify for benefits every two weeks
- View payment details
- Report any work or wages you earn while receiving UI
- Upload additional documents if the EDD asks for them
### Step 5 – Register on **CalJOBS**
- The state requires UI claimants to create a free CalJOBS account and upload a résumé.
- This helps you find new jobs and can keep you eligible for continued benefits.
### Step 6 – Certify Every Two Weeks
- Log in to UI Online (or call the phone system) to **“certify”** that you’re still unemployed or under‑employed.
- If you worked any hours or earned any money, you must report it.
### Step 7 – Receive Your First Payment
- Most people get their first benefit check **within 2–3 weeks** after filing, especially if they use direct deposit.
- If there’s a delay, the EDD will let you know why (missing document, need more info, etc.).
### Step 8 – Keep Your Claim Active
- Continue certifying every two weeks, updating any changes in work, address, or income.
- The EDD may contact you by email, mail, or phone if they need more information.

**Unemployment Insurance** is a temporary cash help for workers in California who lost their job (or had their hours cut) **through no fault of their own**.

## Who Can Get UI? (Eligibility Basics)
You must meet **all** of these rules **when you apply and each week you certify**:
1. **Totally or partially unemployed** – you have no job or only part‑time work.
2. **Lost work through no fault of your own** – e.g., layoff, reduction in hours, fire without cause.
3. **Physically able to work** – you can do a job if one is offered.
4. **Available for work** – you can start a job right away.
5. **Looking for work each week** – you must search and keep records.
6. **Ready and willing to accept suitable work** – if a job fits your skills and pay, you must take it.
> **Note:** Exact rules can vary a little by **county** (for example, how “suitable work” is defined). Your local EDD office will tell you the details that apply to you.

## How the Job‑Search Help Connects to Benefits
1. **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** – After you file an UI claim, the EDD will send you a “Notice of Requirement to Register for Work (DE 8405).” You must:
- Register in **CalJOBS** within **21 days**.
- Keep your resume up‑to‑date and apply to at least one job each week (or attend a training program).
- **Certify** your UI claim each week on myEDD (no later than the due date).

2. **California Training Benefits** – If you enroll in an approved training program (via a community college, trade school, or apprenticeship) **while receiving UI**, you can keep UI payments *and* get a training stipend. Your job‑center counselor can verify that the program qualifies.

3. **CalFresh (Food Assistance)** – Your local county social services office can start a CalFresh application at the same time you visit a Job Center. You’ll need proof of former income (pay stubs or final paycheck) and ID.

4. **CalWORKs (Cash Assistance for Families)** – If you have children and limited income, the county office can evaluate you for CalWORKs. The same staff that help with job placement can give you the forms.

5. **Disability Insurance (DI) & Paid Family Leave (PFL)** – If your layoff was due to a medical condition or you need to care for a family member, the EDD can help you apply for DI or PFL. These are separate from UI but also paid via the same debit‑card system.
## Basic Eligibility Checklist (What Most Programs Look For)

column3: Common Eligibility Points

• Lost job **through no fault of your own** (layoff, reduced hours).
• Able, available, and actively looking for work.
• Earned enough wages in the **past 18 months** (the “base period”).

• Already receiving UI.
• Enrolled in an **EDD‑approved** training or education program.

• Household income ≤ 200 % of the Federal Poverty Level (exact amount varies).
• You must be a California resident and meet citizenship/immigration rules.

• Low‑income family with **children** or a **caretaker** relative.
• Must live in the county where you apply.

• Paid into California’s State Disability Insurance (SDI) program via payroll deductions.
• Sufficient work history and medical certification.

column1: > **Note:** Each of California’s **58 counties** runs its own Social Services Agency. Some counties have extra “rapid‑response” job‑search workshops or additional cash‑assistance pilots. Call or visit your county office to see what special services are offered locally.
## Steps to Get Started (Simple 1‑2‑3)
1. **Apply for Unemployment Insurance (UI) right away**
- Go to **myEDD** or call 1‑800‑300‑5616.
- Have your last employer’s name, address, dates worked, and your most recent pay stub ready.
2. **Visit a Local Job Center (AJCC) within the first week**
- Bring your **UI claim number**, a photo ID, and any résumé you already have.
- Ask the counselor to **register you in CalJOBS** and to check if you qualify for **training benefits**.
3. **Start looking for work or approved training**
- Post your resume in CalJOBS.
- Apply to at least one job each week, or enroll in a qualifying training program.
- Keep a **log of applications** (dates, employer names, contact info) – you’ll need this for UI certification.
4. **Ask about extra assistance**
- While you’re at the Job Center, request **CalFresh** or **CalWORKs** applications if you need food or cash help.
- If you have a disability or need family‑care leave, ask the EDD staff about **DI** or **PFL**.
5. **Certify your UI claim every week**
- Log into **myEDD** each Thursday (or the day shown in your UI notice) and answer the short questionnaire.
- If you miss a week, you could lose that week’s payment.

I’m sorry you’re going through this. Below is a simple guide that explains how **CalFresh (food stamps)** works when you also have **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** or a **severance payment**, and what changes if you move to a different county.
## 1. CalFresh basics

column3: You receive an **Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card** that works like a debit card at any grocery store.

column1: ### Fast‑track help (Emergency CalFresh)
* If you have **no food** or your **income just stopped**, many counties can give you a **one‑time emergency payment** within **5‑7 days** after you apply.
* This is meant to cover you while the regular CalFresh application is being processed (usually 21‑30 days).
**What to do:**
1. Call your **county CalFresh office** and ask for “**Emergency CalFresh**” or “**Rapid Response**”.
2. Fill out the short emergency form (often can be done over the phone or online).
3. Provide any proof you have that your job ended (letter, email, text, or a simple written note with the last work date).
## 2. How UI (unemployment) or severance affects CalFresh

column3: Effect on CalFresh eligibility
column4: What you should tell CalFresh

column3: UI counts as **income**, but you can still qualify as long as the total income is under the CalFresh limit for your household size.
column4: When you first apply, **you do NOT have to report UI** if you haven’t received it yet. Once you start getting UI, **let the county know** so they can recalculate your benefit.

column2: **You have a severance payment** (one‑time lump sum)
column3: A large lump‑sum can raise your monthly income for a short time, which might lower your first‑month CalFresh amount.
column4: Provide the **exact amount** and the **date you received it**. The county will count it only for the month it was received.

column3: Same rule: all money you receive counts toward the income test. As long as the **average monthly income** stays below the limit, you stay eligible.
column4: Report **both** once you have the details. The county can adjust the benefit amount if needed.

column1: **Bottom line:** Receiving UI or a severance **does not automatically disqualify you**. It may change the **amount** of CalFresh you get, but you can still get help.
## 3. Steps to apply for CalFresh (quick guide)
1. **Gather documents** (see section 4).
2. **Apply online** at the state portal:
* **[GetCalFresh.org – Apply Now](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/apply)**
3. **Or call** your county office (search “CalFresh + *your county*”).
4. **Complete the questionnaire** (about 15‑20 minutes).
5. **Submit proof** of income, residency, and identity.
6. **Check status** in the online portal or by calling the county.
*If you request Emergency CalFresh, the county will start a separate fast‑track process right after step 2.*

## 6. What changes if you move to a different county?
* **Eligibility rules are the same statewide**, but some counties have slightly different paperwork or processing speed.
* You must **report the new address** to both **UI (EDD)** and **CalFresh**.
* Most counties will **transfer** your existing CalFresh case, so you usually keep the same benefit amount.
* If you move **before** you receive any CalFresh money, the new county may start a fresh application – ask them if they can “continue” your pending case to avoid a duplicate process.
**Tip:** Call the new county’s CalFresh office as soon as you have a permanent address and ask, “Can you pull my pending application from my old county?”
